story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Well, Jimmy, this is just about to wind up. I sure thank you for this and if you've got any last remarks -- I think we've just about covered everything here.
Well, I do have very strong feelings about behavior, because there is not too much said any more

about how people behave. I have young people come in my house and put their feet up on the table and slouch around, and I have to tell them, you know, you don't sit that way in my house. Get your feet off the table, sit with your feet on the floor, and so forth.

Young people should know that most of the people around are old, they're not young. And they don't like stuff like that. And if you want to get ahead in the world, the -- you've got to learn to -- it's not a matter, even, of because they don't like it. It's because it shows no consideration for other people. And if I have one philosophy, it is I believe in respect. I believe in respect for people and things and I think it isn't too late to put it on.
If anything survives long enough to be here when you're here, that thing deserves respect. I don't care whether it's that table or whether it's me or it's you. That deserves respect. Don't damage it.
That's beautiful. Just say that one more time.

Well, I think that everything that survives has respect because the meaning of life is survival. I know what the meaning of life is, it may sound very silly but the meaning of life is survival. And whatever survives, deserves respect. And whether it's you or me or the table, if you own something, take care of it. If you have a friend,
take care of your friend. If you have a mother and father, take care of your mother and father. But treat everything and everybody with respect.

That's all there is to it. I leave God and everything else to the professionals. I happen to believe in God but that's my private belief. I do believe that everybody should -- whatever survives deserves respect because it's a very simple rule.

It's just a matter of thoughtfulness, you know. As you do things, just watch what you do. You don't have to reform, you don't have to pledge, just be aware of all the time what you're doing, all the time of what you're saying, and you'll do the right thing. I mean, don't pay any attention to what you're doing, you don't pay any attention to what anyone else is doing that you don't do. You don't have to make any great resolutions except go a little bit slower and pay attention to what you're doing and what other people are doing. You automatically, then, will treat everybody with respect, and everything.
